title: Dragon Vein Core
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was about to take Chen Nian away, the ancient inscriptions on the altar suddenly lit up, and the Tianji Record Fragment shuddered violently—it was a reaction it had never shown before.

text.content: That terrifying aura pressed down on his shoulders like something tangible, and every step Chen Ji took felt like treading on the edge of an abyss. The Tianji Record in his embrace grew slightly warm, yet it notably failed to send a warning—as if it too dared not peer into this region. Passing through the final stone door, eroded and riddled with holes by dragon qi, Chen Ji finally beheld the true appearance of the Dragon Vein Core.

It was not the cave or secret realm he had imagined, but an altar emanating a sense of primordial antiquity. Carved from a single block of ink-black mysterious jade, it stood roughly three zhang high, with a stone statue of dragon head on a human body at each of the four corners, lifelike in every detail. At the center of the altar, a translucent pillar of light shot upward, and within it could be discerned a curled-up figure.

That silhouette was so achingly familiar—the same brows, the same eyes, the same contours. Chen Ji had believed he had long sealed away memories of this younger sister in the deepest recesses of his heart, yet now they came flooding forth like a breached dam. He remembered that rainy night a decade ago, when Holy Sect cultivators burst through the door, and how, tugged by his master, he could only watch helplessly as Nian'er was dragged away.

Chen Ji suppressed the churning emotions within him and ascended the altar swiftly. Chen Nian floated silently within the pillar of light, eyes shut tight, her complexion so pallid it bordered on translucent, yet her chest rose and fell with steady breaths—she was actually in a deep slumber. Yet what proved even more unsettling was the astonishing vitality she possessed, like a miniature sun burning within, a vitality that transcended ordinary human limits.

Chen Ji extended his hand, and the moment his fingertips brushed the edge of the light pillar, a violent force surged into his body along his arm. He grunted in pain, yet instead of retreating, he gritted his teeth and pressed his palm against the pillar. The Tianji Record hummed and vibrated, and a warm current of energy gushed forth from the fragment, locking horns with the savage force.

The voice was barely a whisper, yet it exploded in Chen Ji's ears like thunder. His pupils contracted sharply—that was Nian'er's voice! Ten years, the first time in ten years he had heard her speak. Yet just as he was about to call out, a golden pattern suddenly flickered to life at the brow center of the maiden within the light pillar, spreading outward like chains.

Chen Ji's heart seized with alarm; the Tianji Record flashed frantically, warning him of imminent danger—that golden pattern was some kind of seal, and once triggered, the consequences would be unthinkable. He forced himself to remain calm, carefully examining the state of Chen Nian's body. Gradually, he perceived the truth hidden beneath the seal.

It was a fragment of a golden dragon soul, forcibly sealed within Chen Nian's spirit and merged with her vitality. The dragon soul's power continuously nurtured her, yet also resembled a slumbering beast that would turn violent with the slightest provocation. The Holy Sect had refined her into a double-edged sword—simultaneously a vessel and a weapon.

dialogue.content: Take her away, do not awaken her.

text.content: Chen Tianming's voice resounded in his mind, uncharacteristically tinged with anxiety. Chen Ji clenched his fists tightly, his fingernails nearly piercing his palms. Take her away—easy to say. Until the seal is broken, Nian'er cannot wake; but if he attempts to break it, who knew what that dragon soul fragment might do? Moreover, the dragon statues at the altar's four corners were slowly turning, as if observing his every move.

choice.prompt: Faced with the pillar of light seal binding Chen Nian, Chen Ji needed to make a decision. Forcibly breaking the formation might startle the dragon soul, yet without doing so, Nian'er would slumber here forever.

choices.text: Use the Tianji Record to deduce the optimal solution
choices.description: Consume 5 Heavenly Fate points to foresee the optimal path to break the formation within three shichen
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate is inherently precious; is it worth using here?

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, and the Tianji Record Fragment in his palm shuddered violently. A familiar sense of dizziness washed over him, and scenes from the next three shichen flickered past like a carousel. He witnessed his own technique for breaking the formation, saw the dire consequences of the dragon soul running amok, and glimpsed a blurry figure approaching from a distance. Mo Xiansheng had warned him not to employ the Tianji Record unless absolutely necessary. Yet for Nian'er's sake, he was willing to pay any price.

choices.text: Attempt to awaken through bloodline power
choices.description: Chen Ji and Chen Nian share the same lineage; perhaps he could attempt to awaken her through blood resonance
choices.risk_hint: Blood resonance might trigger the seal's应激 reaction

text.content: The blood dripped onto the light pillar, instantly absorbed, stirring an strange resonance in Chen Ji's heart—a bloodline call, a bond of flesh and kin. The pillar trembled, and Chen Nian's eyelashes fluttered, as if sensing something in her dream.

choices.description: Do not act rashly; first investigate the altar's structure and the seal's principles
choices.risk_hint: The aura from afar is approaching; time may be insufficient

text.content: Chen Ji retreated a step, his gaze sweeping across the altar. He noticed the four dragon statues' eyes seemed to follow his movements, and dense inscriptions lined the altar's edges—ancient, powerful characters faintly resembling those on the Tianji Record. The altar's origins were likely far older than he imagined.

Unexpectedly, the inscriptions along the altar's edge glowed with faint fluorescence, writhing like serpents before converging at the altar's center beneath Chen Nian. Chen Ji's pupils constricted—those inscriptions he recognized, ancient sacrificial text from the same source as the Tianji Record. What did this mean? Was there some connection between Chen Nian and the Tianji Record he knew nothing of?

He suppressed his doubts, gaze fixed on his sister. Ten years of separation stretched unbearably long; so much he wished to say, so many questions to ask. Yet she remained in deep slumber, brow creased with pain, lips trembling as if struggling in a nightmare. Chen Ji's heart clenched—for a decade he had schemed across the world, flawless in calculation, yet now felt utterly helpless.

dialogue.content: Nian'er, brother is here to save you. Whatever the cost, I will take you away from here.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji needed to find a way to extract Chen Nian from the altar, but discovered the light pillar and altar were two sides of one entity—forcing it might harm his sister.

choices.text: Attempt to communicate with the Dragon Soul Fragment
choices.description: If the Dragon Soul is sealed within Nian'er, perhaps it can be persuaded
choices.risk_hint: The will of the ancient Dragon Soul far exceeds mortal imagination

text.content: Chen Ji channeled his spiritual sense, carefully probing into the light pillar. He sensed Chen Nian's faint yet tenacious vitality, and beneath it, the slumbering massive presence. It was a remnant of a true ancient Dragon Soul—fragmented, yet still retaining an aura of dominating the world. Chen Ji did not retreat; instead, using the Tianji Record Fragment as a medium, he sent a thought to that Dragon Soul: I am her brother, I've come to take her home.

choices.text: Using Tianji Record inscriptions as a key
choices.description: Since the altar inscriptions share the same origin as the Tianji Record, perhaps they can be used to unseal it
choices.risk_hint: The Tianji Record's reaction exceeded expectations

text.content: Chen Ji took out the Tianji Record Fragment, pressing it against the altar's inscriptions. The fragment burst with dazzling light, forming an strange resonance with the inscriptions. Ancient characters writhed like living things, peeling from the altar and weaving into a complex formation in the air. At the formation's center, a groove slowly appeared, its shape matching the Tianji Record Fragment astonishingly.

Suddenly, that terrifying aura awakening from the dragon vein surged violently, crashing toward the altar like a tide. Chen Ji's hairs stood on end—he sensed some presence watching, an authority far beyond the Heavenly Eye, a realm even the Tianji Record dared not probe. The four dragon statues turned toward him in unison, their empty eye sockets burning with ghostly blue flames.

Chen Ji's heart sank. He had orchestrated schemes across the world for years, priding himself on leaving nothing to chance, yet now he found himself in an unprecedented predicament. Before him lay his sleeping sister, behind him lurked an unknown terror, and the approaching figure in the distance grew increasingly distinct in presence—that was Ling Yuan, the former Sect Master of Tianqing Sect, the dangerous figure who had always hidden in the shadows.

choice.prompt: Multiple threats approached simultaneously, and Chen Ji had to make a decision: should he take his sister first, or stay to face the crisis?

choices.description: Protecting his sister's safety takes absolute priority; everything else can be dealt with later
choices.visible_cost: Might miss out on fortune and opportunity
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan has drawn near, and the presence within the altar's depths is also stirring

text.content: Chen Ji hesitated no more. His hands formed seals, and the Tianji Record Fragment erupted with unprecedented brilliance. Using the fragment as a blade, he hacked open a gap in the pillar of light. The searing radiance stabbed his eyes, his internal qi and blood roiling, yet he clenched his teeth tightly and yanked Chen Nian out of the pillar of light. Ten years had passed—finally, he touched his sister's hand again. That cold yet unmistakably alive sensation made his eyes burn with heat.

choices.text: Stay behind to investigate the truth
choices.description: The connection between the altar inscriptions and the Tianji Record cannot be missed; it must be understood
choices.visible_reward: Might unravel the mysteries of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan has arrived at the altar entrance

text.content: Chen Ji carefully shielded Chen Nian behind him, his gaze fixed intently on the altar's indentation that matched the Tianji Record Fragment. He had an intuition—the complete secrets of the Tianji Record were hidden here. Ling Yuan's presence drew ever closer, but he chose to trust his judgment. The connection between the Tianji Record and this altar, he must understand, even if it meant risking everything.

Just then, a voice—elderly yet full of vitality—resounded from the stone gate. "Chen Ji, I never expected you to actually find this place." Ling Yuan strode into the altar, his gray-white hair floating in the dragon's qi, his eyes shimmering with complex light. He glanced at Chen Nian suspended beside the pillar of light, then looked at the Tianji Record Fragment in Chen Ji's hand, a meaningful smile curling at his lips. "It seems this old man has arrived at just the right moment."

Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged, but his mind raced with calculations. Ling Yuan had come too quickly—too quickly to be mere coincidence. This meant either the altar's upheaval had alarmed him, or... someone had tipped him off. On the surface, he still maintained that pathetic, humble facade, yet beneath his eyes lay only cold calculation. Ten years had passed—this old fox could finally no longer restrain himself.

Ling Yuan stepped closer, his gaze always fixed on the Tianji Record Fragment, the greed and covetousness in his eyes almost entirely unconcealed. "This old man also participated in the Tianji Record's selection back then, but it rejected me." His voice was calm, yet carried years of suppressed resentment, "Who would have thought that in the end, it would choose a waste like you." The dragon statues at the altar's four corners still watched them, the dragon soul fragments within Chen Nian stirringslightly, as if issuing a warning.

Chen Ji raised his head; for the first time, that pair of usually calm eyes displayed a sharp edge. "Where does the Former Sect Master speak of? The Tianji Record chose whom it chose—that is Heaven's will." His voice remained indifferent, yet carried an undetectable hint of mockery, "If you have come to reminisce, your disciple will keep you company; if you have come to take things by force..." He did not finish, but the meaning was abundantly clear. Chen Nian in his arms still slumbered; he had to end this quickly. The ancient inscriptions on the altar behind him flickered silently, emanating a tempting yet dangerous glow.

Ling Yuan burst into laughter, the sound filled with mockery and triumph. "With you?" He swept his sleeve, and a majestic pressure like an endless sea instantly engulfed the entire altar—that was Nascent Soul late stage cultivation, the accumulated heritage of Tianqing Sect for hundreds of years. "This old man has waited for this day far too long. The Tianji Record, the incomplete prophetic ability, and..." His gaze fell upon Chen Nian, a flash of greed in his eyes, "the Heavenly Fate Lock Key. Today, this old man shall claim them all." Chen Ji's eyes darkened, and he shielded Chen Nian even more tightly; he already had a plan forming.

Ling Yuan advanced step by step, each step carrying the momentum to destroy worlds. However, the instant he stepped into the altar's center, the dragon statues at the four corners simultaneously spewed golden pillars of light, trapping him in place. Ling Yuan's expression changed drastically; he struggled wildly yet to no avail. The ancient seal of the altar fully activated at this moment, like a giant beast awakening, beginning to turn against all intruders. Chen Ji held Chen Nian tightly, using the dragon statues' attacks as cover, and spotted an opportunity to approach the inscriptions at the altar's edge—perhaps there lay the only chance for survival.
